milestones.name: Parallel smoke solver loops with pinned reference hashes
milestones.validation: Per-cell loops (advection, boundary conditions, forces, pressure operator, vector updates, gradient subtraction, divergence check, field validation, source injection) run on rayon with every element written by the same expression as before; reductions stay serial and in index order. Final-state hashes of reference scenarios recorded before the change still match, and are equal on 1, 2 and 8 rayon threads. The pressure operator reads a precomputed open-face mask, two reductions share one pass, the step copies only the evolving fields (density, temperature, velocity), and trilinear sampling has an exact in-range path compared bit for bit with the original on about 240,000 points. A failed step leaves the committed state and clock untouched: injected failures in the collider stage, field validation and the pressure solve, then a corrected retry equals a fresh replay. Advection at 128^3 on one thread, impact scene: 1650-1770 ms before the sampling change, 1423 ms after (measured under load).
milestones.limits: Timings were measured on a loaded machine and only on x86_64 Linux, not certified. The reference hashes hold only on that platform. The Jacobi mode keeps serial in-order reductions, so its pressure solve does not scale with threads like the other loops. No GPU render of the faster solver was run for this entry. Timings measured on a quiet machine are in quiet_machine_timing_validation.

milestones.name: Multigrid-preconditioned pressure solve
milestones.validation: Conjugate-gradient projection preconditioned by one algebraic-aggregation V(1,1) cycle (2x2x2 aggregates, Galerkin operator, symmetric red-black Gauss-Seidel, coarse correction scaled by 1.5, dense Cholesky on at most 128 cells), with reductions over fixed 2048-cell blocks combined by a fixed binary tree. Tests: V-cycle symmetry and positivity with and without solids, exact Galerkin products, direct solve and mean removal on floating components, sealed fluid pockets (closed, open and expanding: an expanding pocket still fails with a pressure error because the removed mean stays in the final divergence check), equal results on 1, 2 and 8 threads with pinned hashes, iteration counts against resolution, and agreement with the Jacobi solver when both converge tightly. Measured on the impulse step at 128^3: Jacobi 275 iterations, multigrid 14.
milestones.limits: Convergence is judged by the RMS divergence over all fluid cells, so an error confined to a few cells of a large domain can pass. Multigrid results differ from Jacobi in the last bits, and the reference hashes hold only on x86_64 Linux. Iteration counts are not timings: no wall-time benefit is certified, and the solver has no visual review on the impact film.

milestones.name: MacCormack advection with an extrema limiter
milestones.validation: Backward-forward error correction (Selle et al., 2008) for density, temperature and the three velocity components, clamped to the minimum and maximum of the eight old values around the backward-trace origin and falling back to the semi-Lagrangian value where a collider cuts a trace. Free vortex (32^3 closed box, 60 force-free steps, multigrid): kinetic energy kept 96.6% against 68.8% and enstrophy 95.7% against 61.6% for semi-Lagrangian advection; the test requires 1.25x and 1.3x of the semi-Lagrangian values and energy that never grows. A swirling blob against a wall creates no new density or temperature extrema and leaves solid cells clean; results are equal on 1, 2 and 8 threads, with pinned hashes. The impact scene ran 144 steps at 64^3 and 128^3 without error.
milestones.limits: The advection stage measured 2.5x (64^3) and 2.4x (128^3) the semi-Lagrangian time on one thread, measured on a loaded machine and only on x86_64 Linux, not certified. Velocity uses the scheme on the strength of one vortex test; no visual comparison on the impact film was made. Hashes hold only on x86_64 Linux. Timings measured on a quiet machine are in quiet_machine_timing_validation.

milestones.name: Smoke memory estimate and resident state size
milestones.validation: The step memory estimate fell from 512 to 320 and then to 288 bytes per cell plus 8192, from a count of the live arrays (committed state 41, working state 41, solid-face list 56 if every cell were solid, pressure workspace 65, multigrid about 26), and a test pins the figure. Prescribed solid face velocities left the state, which now holds about 41 bytes per cell independent of colliders (a test checks 40-43 bytes per cell and that a step with a collider does not grow it); 30, 3 and 1 states fit 256 MiB at 64x52x64, 128x104x128 and 192x156x192 (14, 1 and none before). Reference hashes of both pressure solvers and both advection schemes pass unchanged. The least budgets the constructor accepts at those three resolutions were found by running it and are tabulated in the SREP. Peak resident memory on the impact scene (6 steps, multigrid, no colliders): 326 MB at 128x104x128 and 928 MB at 192x156x192.
milestones.limits: Peak resident memory depends on the allocator and on untouched pages, and was measured on a loaded machine and only on x86_64 Linux, not certified. milestones.name: Cheaper smoke volume export, cache key and checkpoints
milestones.validation: The five volume channels build in parallel and store whole 8x8x8 bricks (SparseGrid::set_brick, equivalent to 512 single sets and atomic on failure); the exported volume is identical to the previous implementation, compared bit for bit on five reference cases (colliders, odd and closed domains) and two temperature backgrounds. A volume is neither exported nor hashed when the simulation state did not change: four samples inside a fixed step return the same volume, a new step exports once, and a backward seek exports again and reproduces the first visit's key. The cache key hashes each brick on its own and combines the hashes in key order, so it is the same for any thread count; a flipped mantissa bit, swapped samples, another name or background, and 3000 single-voxel variations change it. Impact scene after 8 steps on a busy machine: export 610 to 77-100 ms at 128^3 and 2.2 s to 150-165 ms at 192^3; hashing 70 to 3 ms at 128^3 and 254 to 21 ms at 192^3; cloning a 192^3 state for a checkpoint took 102 ms.
milestones.limits: Timings were measured under load (load average about 12-14) on x86_64 Linux and are not certified. The key is an in-memory cache token whose values changed; no stored key and no test compares it with a fixed value. The dense velocity channels still dominate export time. Timings measured on a quiet machine are in quiet_machine_timing_validation.

milestones.name: Second-order ocean with a monotonized-central limiter
milestones.validation: Spec::order selects first order (default; a digest of the frame bits recorded from the earlier solver is unchanged for closed, open and periodic edges) or second order: MUSCL reconstruction of surface elevation and velocity with the monotonized-central limiter, depth-capped so face depths stay non-negative, first order at wet/dry fronts and non-periodic edge cells, SSP-RK2, a time-step bound halved to 0.225 and Strang-split drag. Amplitude lost by a 1e-3 wave after five wavelengths (order 1 / order 2): 99.96% / 77.2% at 10 cells per wavelength, 97.9% / 17.9% at 20, 85.3% / 2.6% at 40, 61.7% / 0.34% at 80. The minmod and van Leer limiters lost more at 10 and 20 cells (97.4% and 64.1%; 88.2% and 31.1%) and the choice rests on that comparison. Rest on rough bathymetry (to 1e-12), conservation on closed and periodic edges, positivity on wet/dry fronts over rough beaches, replay after checkpoint eviction and equality on 1, 2 and 8 threads pass in both orders.
milestones.limits: The bed-source term stays first order: second order holds for waves over a smooth bed. Non-negative depth at the 0.225 bound is verified by tests and not proven for the unsplit two-dimensional scheme; negative depth beyond round-off could not be provoked. Ten cells per wavelength still lose 77%, so waves need at least 20 cells per wavelength; the flux stays local Lax-Friedrichs. An absorbing edge (relaxation layer) was built and not adopted: for smooth pulses the zero-gradient open edge already reflects little (about 0% in one dimension, 3-7% against free space for a finite beam) and the layer reflected no less. Digests hold only on x86_64 Linux.

milestones.name: Ejecta thrown out by an impact: driver births in the 3D particle solver and burst@crater
milestones.validation: The 3D particle Driver can give, per fixed step window, births with exact instant, position, velocity and mass (mass kept in the particle); the 7 tests of particles3d_births cover birth at the exact instant, reverse replay and checkpoint budgets, ids and order among rate and burst births, no change for emitters that give none, an error and not a truncation above maxParticles with the published frame kept, windows asked once going forward, and births outside the window refused. milestones.name: Per-body water samples and owner tags in the ocean solver
milestones.validation: With Spec::body_owners the driver tags every occupied column with the body that holds most of it, and at each completed canonical step, next to Forcing::exchange, the driver is offered per body: the momentum that body gave the water in the step, the least-squares plane through the free surface of the wet columns of its footprint (level at the centre and two slopes), the depth-weighted mean horizontal water velocity, and the mean bed ordinate. The 7 tests of ocean_owners check that the per-body impulses add up to the total exchange to rounding, that a single body gave what all gave, bit-identical samples on replay with and without checkpoints (first and second order), that tagging does not change the water, an exact plane through a sloped surface (level, both slopes, velocity, bed) and no slope along a direction without extent, and the errors for an unknown tag and for tags without bodies; one evaluator test checks that two spheres and a crater surface in the colliders list tag their columns with their place in it. sr-sim, sr-model and sr-eval pass; clippy -D warnings and fmt clean.
milestones.limits: The solver delivers the samples; no consumer (reaction on the body, buoyancy from the perturbed surface) exists yet. A column held by several bodies is credited whole to the one with most of it. The tags cost 12 bytes per cell and 16 per body per checkpoint, charged only when body_owners is non-zero; the evaluator now sets it for every ocean that has body colliders, so those oceans are charged 12 bytes per cell more. Run time of the extra work (one owner pass and one footprint scan per canonical step) was measured on a 720x720 second-order ocean (the hero-hires grid) with a body of 1600 cells, 4 threads, on a machine at load 9 to 10, five alternating runs of 8 steps (examples/ocean_bodies_profile.rs): 1.130 s per step without tags and 1.203 s with them (about 6%), but the runs overlap (the last pair is inverted), so the cost is between nothing and about 10%, not resolved on this loaded machine. The hero-hires scene itself was not run for this entry.

milestones.name: Recent steps kept by the 3D particle emitter, for the samples of a motion-blur shutter
milestones.validation: A motion-blurred frame asks the evaluator for the frame and then for the shutter's samples (the first, the last, then each in turn), so the emitter is asked for a step ahead and then for steps behind it; each request that went back across a step restored the last checkpoint (up to a second of fixed steps earlier) and replayed from it. The emitter now also keeps its latest fixed steps (a quarter of checkpointMemoryMiB at most, none unless that holds three states, counted together with the checkpoints) and restarts from the latest stored state at or before the target, whichever kind. examples/blur_profile.rs asks a scene the way the renderer's sub-frame source does (40 frames from 2 s, 16 samples, 180 degree shutter, 20000 particles, step 1/120 s, a collider floor and a rigid ball): the 16 shutter samples cost 25.0 s of wall time per 40 frames before and 9.3 s after (the same scene with one sample: 1.1 to 2.0 s), and the combined hash of the particle frames was equal before and after, in the first scene (6000 particles, step 1/24 s, whose samples all lie inside one step, 2.8 s) as in this one. Tests (3, particles3d_recent): a sample that goes back replays no step with the recent steps against about 300 windows without them, frames equal to those of an emitter that keeps nothing, any scrubbing order agrees with a fresh emitter, and checkpoints plus recent steps stay within the budget for budgets from 1 KiB to 256 MiB.
milestones.limits: What remains is one partial step of every particle per distinct sample time (about 14 ms for 20000 particles on this loaded machine), which the exact frame at that instant needs; it grows with the number of samples. Measured on a loaded machine (load 8 to 14), only on this scene and on x86_64 Linux. No GPU render was run, and the sub-frame source of the renderer was imitated at the evaluator, not exercised.

milestones.name: Cavity of a body entering the water: waterImpulse@source and driver events in the ocean solver
milestones.validation: The solver takes impulses from the driver per canonical step (Forcing::events, those whose instant lies in (T - dt, T] at the sample that ends the step at T, validated and applied among the substeps in order of time after authored impulses of the same instant) and a Cavity impulse kind that moves the wanted volume or 90% of what its central disc holds, whichever is less, so it is limited by the water layer and never an error for lack of water. waterImpulse source=body (OCN10 to OCN12 in Schematron and Rust, 4 new corpus documents, oracle agreement with 279 documents) makes the cavity of the first entry of a dynamic body listed in colliders: the instant from the lowest point of its poses at the two ends of each step, the place under its centre, the volume and radius from the water row of the cratering law with its mass, its density (mass over the volume of its closed surface), its downward speed and the ocean's gravity. 7 solver tests (ocean_events): wanted volume moved from the disc to the ring with all the water kept, the limit and the failure of a negative displace in the same case, a dry or unresolved place does nothing, a driver-given impulse equal bit for bit to the authored one at the same instant (orders 1 and 2, three instants), nothing before the instant and identical replay with and without checkpoints, errors for an impulse outside its step or at the first sample, and a driver that asks for nothing changes nothing. 6 evaluator tests (water_entry): nothing before the entry and a change at it with a depression at the entry point, all the water kept, the far wave of the cavity alone (the difference with and without it) growing with speed (0.0033, 0.0071, 0.0170 for 10, 20, 30 m/s) and with mass (0.0024, 0.0071, 0.0207 for 500, 2000, 8000 kg), no cavity for a body that starts in the water, enters outside the ocean or moves away, shallow water neither an error nor an emptied column, and the same water after scrubbing and on a fresh evaluator. sr-sim, sr-model and sr-eval: 628 passed, 0 failed, 7 ignored; clippy -D warnings and fmt clean.
milestones.limits: The combined far wave, with the body's own occupancy, is not monotone in speed in these runs (0.0326, 0.0390, 0.0276 at 10, 20, 30 m/s in 100 m of water): cavity and occupancy have opposite signs near the entry point and partly cancel, so the cavity alone does not give a wave that grows with the energy; the horizontal reaction on the body is not here. Only the first entry of a body makes a cavity; the cavity forms at once, not over the law's formation time, and is applied at the entry instant for the body's pose at the step ends; a disc smaller than four cells is widened with its volume kept. The law is that of a crater in water, not a validated model of water entry, and the model is hydrostatic with no jet or spray. The CLI and GPU were not run for this entry.

milestones.name: Ejecta of a growing crater land on its ground: births clear of the surface and a limit of their own for penetration recovery
milestones.validation: With the ground as the collider of burst@crater ejecta the 3D particle solver stopped with 'more than 16 collisions in one particle step' at 1.6 s of the land impact. Every one of those contacts was at fraction 0 (no time advanced): the impact point lies about 0.1 m inside the surface, so ejecta were born buried and pushed under the one-sided sheet (a particle then chased a floor sinking at 11 m/s), and a particle between two steep facets of the crater was pushed out of each in turn by a factor of about 0.3 per push, needing about 25 pushes to reach the contact tolerance. Ejecta of a crater are now born clear of the surface along the geometric normal of the owner by their largest collision radius plus the contact tolerance, and the solver counts contacts at fraction 0 apart from the 16 that move time forward, with a limit of 64 and its own error ('more than 64 penetration recoveries in one particle step'). milestones.name: Null geodesics of a Schwarzschild black hole and a CPU reference image of it
milestones.validation: sr_sim::gr (commits 7a5084c API and tests, d68474b integrator, 5e33e9d oracle, 03e8eee, c7fcc13; gr::image 5269eee, bc4e7d1, 28799fd; 2026-10-06; the results are deterministic and do not depend on the load): the classical Runge-Kutta integration in phi of u'' = -u + 3 M u^2 with the fixed step 0.02 and at most 4096 steps (the shader's), capture at u >= 1/(2M), escape at u <= 0 with a linear interpolation of the angle, crossings of the planes phi0 + k pi by shortening the step; the same code in f32 (gr::f32); closed forms and quadratures in gr::oracle (shadow sqrt(27) M, horizon, photon sphere, 6M, Kepler Omega, turning point by bisection, exact deflection by Romberg quadrature of the integral rewritten with a smooth integrand, weak-field series to the fourth order, Luminet's redshift, Shakura-Sunyaev temperature). Tests (sr-sim, gr 10 of 10, gr_image 6 of 6): the impact parameter that separates capture from escape for a ray from 1e9 M is within a relative 9.7e-8, 5.7e-9, 3.5e-10, 2.1e-11 of sqrt(27) M at the steps 0.08, 0.04, 0.02, 0.01 (the asked-for bound was 1e-4); the integrated deflection at the step 2e-4 is 0.590395778, 0.236135975 and 0.041222440 against the quadrature's 0.590395788, 0.236135995 and 0.041222540 at b = 10, 20, 100 M (asked 1e-5; the 1e-7 at 100 M is the part of the ray before 1e9 M); the angle at infinity at the shader's step 0.02 is within 1.3e-7 of the quadrature for b = 5.3, 5.5, 6, 8, 10, 20, 100 M (7.2e-8 at 10 M; 4.8e-8 at 5.3 M); the error at b = 10 M falls 9.1e-7, 7.2e-8, 6.1e-9 for the steps 0.04, 0.02, 0.01 (a ratio of about 12, below 16 because the final angle is a linear interpolation); the weak-field series to the fourth order leaves a residual of about 700 (M/b)^5 (1291, 919, 750 at b = 10, 20, 100 M); single against double precision, for four rays, at most 9.4e-7 relative in the angle at infinity and 1.4e-5 in the radius of a crossing; the step of the RK4 is symmetric in phi to the bit and a ray from the turning point sweeps half of the whole deflection to 1e-5; the same arguments give the same bits. The image (gr::image, with the convention of the shader's geodesic.wgsl at 9ec682d written in its doc): on 256 x 160 pixels with an equatorial camera at 40 M and a focal length of 100 pixels the shadow is 12.915 px by area against 12.764 px expected (limit 0.5), the captured pixels are the ones inside the expected radius; the left and right halves of an inclined image have the same classes, orders and radii (1e-9) and 1/g + 1/g' averages to 1/sqrt(1 - 3M/r) to 1e-9; the column through the plane of the axis has g = sqrt(1 - 3M/r) to 1e-12; a face-on disk is black in the middle, then the disk as it is seen with the radius growing outward, then higher orders, then the sky. A first note of mine in the report on this work gave the error of the angle at the shader's step as about 1e-3: that was the bound the test first used, not a measurement; the measured one is the 1.3e-7 above and the bound is now 1e-6. The shader against gr::image (the renderer's test, sr-gpu commits e4b1f85 tests and 99f4d2e shader, NVIDIA adapter, 2026-10-06, as its author reported it; not rerun here): on 96 x 60 pixels, f32 on the GPU against f64, 5760 of 5760 pixels have the same class (106 captured, 5084 background, 570 disk); the worst relative difference is 1.2e-5 in the angle of escape, 8.1e-6 in the radius of the point of the disk, 3.1e-6 in g and 1.3e-6 rad in the azimuth. Against gr::f32::trace for rays more than 5% from the critical curve, 2528 of 3186 crossing radii agree to 1e-6 or better, the worst is 1.2e-5 up to 56 M (6.8e-5 beyond, near the escape) and 1.4e-6 in the angle of escape: the GPU compiler contracts operations and the bits do not match. The shadow of an observer at 1e4 M is 39.99 px for the 40 expected.
milestones.limits: Schwarzschild only, in the plane of each ray; the disk is a single thin opaque plane and only the first four crossings of its plane are followed; the fixed step and the 4096 steps make a ray that circles the photon sphere for more than about 82 rad a capture; the exact deflection loses accuracy within a few per cent of b_c; the redshift exists for r > 3M; the time of an image turns the pattern of the disk and not r, psi or g, so the reference does not take it. milestones.name: Smoke that the impact of a crater causes (`pyroSource@crater` and `pyroImpulse@crater`)
milestones.validation: A pyroSource or pyroImpulse with crater naming a crater that grows from an impact emits the smoke the impact makes, with no time, place or amount authored. Engine and solver (c67ffba, 2026-10-04): cratering::smoke gives the dust as dustFraction of the volume thrown out, the heat as heatFraction of (1/2) m U^2 sin(theta)^(3/2), and the temperature rise as heat over dust mass times specificHeat, capped at maxTemperature (defaults 0.1, 0.01, 1000 J/(kg K), 5000 K); the solver derives the expansion of heated sources as an ideal gas at constant pressure, (dT/dt)/T. Tests: pyro_heat (7) checks the divergence against dT/(T dt) to 1e-7 relative, equality with an authored source of that expansion, one-shot impulses, refusal of an authored expansion on a heated source, unchanged unheated sources, and dust as a total over free cells (total 256 to 1e-9); cratering (5 smoke tests) checks dust, heat and rise against the formulas to 1e-12 relative, monotone growth with speed, mass and angle, rise under 20 K for a slow impact, the cap at 5000 and 1200 K, and the defaults. Schema (9c7af61, 2026-10-04): rules PYC1 to PYC4, tested by the 5 tests of pyro_crater, one valid and four invalid corpus files. Evaluator (968c277, 2026-10-04), 10 tests in crater_smoke: no dust before it; dust within 20 % of the law at 60, 100 and 150 m/s, growing with speed and mass; temperature rise above 0.5 and below 1.05 times the law's; heating changes the flow; an impulse fires once; any order, a fresh evaluator and a baked physics cache agree bit for bit; each symbol instance has its own smoke. Later fixes: a15a596 and 09ef11c (2026-10-04) make the dust a total over free cells, so with the ground as a collider the most dust is 0.0207 cubic metres for the law's 0.0219 where half was lost before; both runs are asserted within 20 %; fe8287c (2026-10-04) takes the crater axis from the surface normal (normal speed 86.63 m/s for the authored 86.6); 59af91a and 4fbc5be (2026-10-06) fail the smoke when the rigid world cannot answer and share the clock probe. In the impact_scenes test (commit e22458b, 2026-10-05, deterministic) the rise at 30, 60 and 90 degrees is 19.20, 19.07 and 19.08 K.
milestones.limits: Only dust heated by the impact and spread through the crater volume is represented; the vapour, melt and shock wave that make a real fireball are not, and the defaults are not to be tuned to make fire. The share of an impact's energy that rises in smoke has no published value, so heatFraction, dustFraction and specificHeat are the engine's own and uncalibrated; the sin^(3/2) angle scaling is that of hydrocode runs, not a measurement here. In physical units a slow impact barely heats anything and a 20 km/s impact of 1500 kg heats its dust by only a few hundred kelvin (the test asserts between 100 and 5000 K; no exact value was recorded). The temperature rise is nearly flat in angle. The smoke needs the composition clock and a uniformly scaled volume, begins at the first smoke step after the impact, and a sealed domain cannot sustain the expansion. The ocean scene has no smoke from its crater. No timing was recorded for this item.

milestones.name: A fracture that an impact sets off: `fracture@source`
milestones.validation: A fracture can name the dynamic rigid body that breaks it (fracture@source, with minImpulse and energyFraction); the body breaks at the first impact of the source on it, found by the rigid world's impact watch, and nothing in the document says when. Commits 7989b29, 7eaf768, 2820484, cc5f69b, 2cf1fa2 and 14d7aea, all 2026-10-06. The push is one speed along every line out of the centre of mass, the mass-weighted mean taken off, with E = f * 1/2 mu v_n^2 (mu the reduced mass, v_n the closing speed). The mean removal is a fix: before 7989b29 an asymmetric partition (pieces of 1, 2 and 3 kg) gained momentum, and the_radial_impulse_adds_no_linear_momentum_to_an_asymmetric_partition failed with 'momentum added along 0: [-0.9867990671453821, -2.680415860774205, 1.8862159038238724e-17]'; after 7989b29 it asserts linear and angular momentum added under 1e-9. sr-sim fracture_contact: nothing breaks before the impact and the fracture fires on the step after it is noticed, no sooner; the pieces' momentum equals the target's to 1e-9 and the energy gained equals the closed form to 1e-6 of itself (90.000000 against 90.000000 in the SREP); a_weak_impact_and_no_impact_break_nothing (threshold 1e6, a projectile at rest); the_same_pieces_in_any_order_of_requests_and_from_a_fresh_world compares bits; a_contact_that_names_no_watch_of_the_body_is_refused. sr-eval fracture_contact has four tests (breaks at the impact and not before, 4 pieces of total mass 8 within 1e-9; weak or no impact; same pieces in any order of frames and from a baked cache; a fracture at a time is as it was), and a physcache test keeps the cache identity of a world with a fracture at a time. Schema: FRX5 to FRX7 in the Schematron and in rules.rs with five invalid and two valid corpus documents; build_corpus.py checks every document against lxml and the manifest lists 279 invalid and 47 valid documents (274 and 45 before). Block scene (impact_block, four tests): 12 pieces, mass within 1e-6 of 583200 kg, still until the contact, distance rising with speed and mass; mean distance of the pieces at 3 s 6.3, 10.5, 14.5 m for 60, 100, 150 m/s and 7.4, 10.5, 11.4 m for 30, 90, 270 t; deterministic.
milestones.limits: The energy fraction 0.3 is the engine's value and has no published source. The push is a modelled quantity, not a measured one, and the block distances are orders of magnitude and directions, not predictions of a real impact. The partition does not depend on where the impact was; only the push (speed and masses) and the owner's spin tell cases apart. A piece does not break again (no second generation). The source is not part of the partition, and one that has penetrated the owner by more than a step's travel may overlap pieces until the solver pushes it out. The push adds E to energy the contact has already treated; the engine does not check that f is at most 1 - e^2 for the pair's restitution e. It is a cinematic cut, not a stress or toughness model. The spreads were measured on one scene. No cost figure and no counts of the whole test suite were recorded for these commits.

milestones.name: Smoke drags the particles that name it: `particles3D@gas`
milestones.validation: An emitter that names a smoke volume with gas adds drag times the smoke's velocity at the particle's place and time to its acceleration, so the closed-form flight obeys p'' = k (u - v) plus gravity and fields; the gas is the linear interpolation of the two smoke steps around the instant. Commits fc3e462 (the gas copied out of a smoke step), a74cd40 (schema, rule P3D11, corpus), 0897b84 and 0c9df98 (evaluator; one gas context per canonical particle step), all 2026-10-04; later fixes fe207a9, 11b4a90 (2026-10-04) and 8c3ed9b (2026-10-06). Tests in pyro_gas: inside the domain the copy's velocity_at equals the state's own to the last bit, open and closed; outside it falls to rest across one cell (largest change in a thousandth of a cell under 0.005 of the face speed, exactly 0 beyond one cell, a non-finite point at rest); a copy does not follow the simulation. Tests in particles_gas: the particle follows the integral of k (u - v) against the gas's own history, read from a follower of drag 40, to within 3 % in velocity and position at 1.2, 1.5 and 2.0 s; without the reference, with drag 0, or 500 units away the bits are those of the document without it; the particle goes farther with the gas's speed and with the drag; any order of frames, a fresh evaluator and a smoke with checkpointMemoryMiB 1 give the same bits; a particle that leaves the volume only slows and never changes by more than k times the gas speed times the step; a frame between two canonical steps asks 1 to 8 queries and simulates no smoke step; a moving volume drags where it is; a failing or over-budget smoke fails the particles by name, 16 MiB refusing and 20 MiB admitting seventeen fields (14.3 MB) and two kept states (2.7 MB). Test gas_and_splash: ejecta dragged by a smoke that fall into an ocean simulate the smoke once per step (30 steps in 3 s where 69 had been, 8c3ed9b). Fixtures: valid/particles3d-gas.scene.xml and invalid/p3d11-gas.scene.xml. Cost (ignored test cost_of_the_gas_per_particle_step, release, one core, 20 000 particles, 25 steps): 0.77 s over naming the gas with no drag, 1.5 microseconds per particle step against 7 at first (0c9df98).
milestones.limits: The coupling is linear in the relative velocity and one way: the particles do not push the gas. For 0.34 m rocks of 2100 kg/m3 at 50 m/s relative the quadratic drag is a rate of about 0.03 per second (computed from the drag law, not measured), so it moves dust-sized particles or an authored drag, not the ejecta of the impact scenes. The driver is asked one particle at a time, so the coupling is serial; the load of the machine at the cost measurement was not recorded, and 22 s for 100 000 particles over a 6 s film is an extrapolation, not measured. The agreement with the gas history was only checked on a pushed open box of 32 cells. After 8c3ed9b the particles run before the smoke, but the schema documentation and the SREP text still say the smoke is simulated before them.

milestones.validation: Commits 574d621 and 2afdecd (the same change on two branches), 2026-10-04. The in-volume shadow march sampled the density grid at every step although most of the domain holds a decayed tail of tiny values. A per-volume map of 4-voxel cells, built on the CPU, marks the cells whose readable voxels could add more than 1e-10 to the optical depth along any ray (the largest density times density scale times extinction times the longest path in the domain; about 300 times under half an ulp of an f32 near 1); the march jumps over the others. milestones.name: A simulation that cannot run is an error of the frame
milestones.validation: Commit 91e9013, 2026-10-04. A solver that hit a resource limit or failed during evaluation was recorded as a problem and the renderer turned every problem into a note: smoke and ocean failed with derived messages that hid the cause ("volume primitive requires @volume", "ocean evaluation produced no surface"), while 3D particles and fracture over their budget vanished from the frame and the render still succeeded unless --strict was given. The frame graph now carries failures, the part of the problems that are simulations authored but unable to run (smoke, ocean, 3D particles, fracture, and the crater and collider limits of a rigid body); the renderer reports each as an error, drops the derived messages of a node whose simulation failed, and keeps authorised fallbacks as notes; the command line prints every error and the notes when it exits on one, and delivery reports all of them. Test crates/scene-render/tests/solver_failures.rs, seven cases (smoke over its memory, the ocean's solver and its surface over their memory, 3D particles over their budget, a crater's draw vertices over the memory budget, the collider of a rigid body's crater, a fracture over its budget): render, render --strict, render --bench and encode each exit 1, name the cause, do not print the derived message and leave no image; and a fracture released at 0.5 s whose budget is checked when the world is built is reported at time 0.
milestones.limits: Only the simulations listed are failures: other problems stay notes, and authorised fallbacks stay notes. The tests run the command line on the host's default adapter; the reports of delivery (overlay and pipeline) have no test of their own in that commit.

milestones.name: The renderer's geodesic pass and the camera with geodesics
milestones.validation: Commits 99f4d2e (the pass), 74ebc2d (the pattern of the disk), 7df721d (the camera in the 3D pass), e4b1f85 (the references), 2026-10-06, NVIDIA RTX 6000 Ada through the GPU queue, release, deterministic. The pass draws a whole frame from a hole of mass M, an optional thin Keplerian disk and a star field: each ray is integrated from the observer in the plane of the ray (u'' = -u + 3 M u^2, RK4 in the angle, step 0.02 rad, at most 4096 steps), the last step before each crossing of the disk's plane (phi0 + k pi) is shortened to land on it, a ray is captured, escapes to a direction that indexes the stars, or meets the disk (opaque, first of the first four crossings inside its radii); the disk emits a blackbody at g T with g = sqrt(1 - 3M/r) / (1 + Omega b h) and a seeded pattern turned by the Keplerian rate; the camera with geodesics="true" draws the document's blackHole and accretionDisk (exposure, pathSamples as rays per pixel, sRGB encoding of the working space) and anything else of the 3D scene under it is an error. Tests of crates/sr-gpu/tests/geodesic.rs (11) and geodesic_scene.rs (3): the shadow of an observer 1e4 M away is 5024 pixels, a radius of 39.990 px for 40.000 expected (limit 1 px); a disk seen along its axis is left-right symmetric and g = sqrt(1 - 3M/r) to 2e-4; in the weak field (M = 0.05 at 200) g is within 4e-3 of 1 / (1 + v.d) over more than 300 pixels with the side that turns toward the camera blueshifted; at 75 degrees there are 210 pixels of the second image above the shadow and 1408 below; against an f64 integration written in the test, 2560 rays: worst relative error in the escape angle 4.5e-5 and in the radius of the first two crossings 4.9e-5 (9.4e-4 for the later ones, which are ill-conditioned along a ray near the critical curve); against the CPU reference image of sr_sim::gr (96 x 60, camera at 60 M and 75 degrees): 5760 of 5760 pixels have the same class (106 captured, 5084 background, 570 disk) and the worst relative errors are 1.2e-5 in the escape angle, 8.1e-6 in the radius of the disk point, 3.1e-6 in g and 1.3e-6 rad in the azimuth; against the single-precision reference integrator, for rays more than 5 % from the critical impact parameter, 2528 of 3186 crossing radii are within 1e-6, the worst 1.2e-5 up to 56 M and 6.8e-5 beyond, the worst escape angle 1.4e-6; the pattern at geometric time 40 against the closed form of spiral arms: 2560 pixels to 4.4e-6 (the largest change a factor of 10); no pixel is not finite in four output modes; bands of 7 rows equal the whole frame bit for bit; the same seed gives the same picture. Breaking the sign of the rotation (g 0.9934 against 1.0026 at one pixel) or the term 3 M u^2 to 2 M u^2 (a shadow of 26.7 px against 40) fails them. In a document: a hole seen almost along the axis has a black opaque shadow with nothing bright inside 0.8 of the 15.2 px of its radius; the pattern turns with the time of the frame (2532 pixels differ between t = 0 and 3) and a smooth disk does not (0); a hole under an ordinary camera draws nothing and says so. Cost, median of 7 frames with the read-back: 320 x 200 1.0 ms at 16 rays per pixel and 3.2 ms at 64; 1280 x 800 4.3 ms at 16, 8.5 ms at 32, 17.0 ms at 64. A 30 s film at 1280 x 800 and 64 rays (720 frames) rendered in 78.7, 90.1 and 90.1 s for 240 frames each, its 320 x 200 pixel-art version in 10.7, 9.2 and 8.5 s.
milestones.limits: The disk is opaque, thin and flat, and a ray follows only four crossings of its plane; the background is a procedural star field at infinity (no environment map); the fixed step and the 4096 steps make a ray that circles the photon sphere for more than about 82 rad a capture. The shader is f32 and the compiler contracts and rounds the operations: 1e-6 against the f32 reference is not reached for every ray (2528 of 3186 radii), and crossings beyond a few disk radii or after a winding are ill-conditioned. The camera needs a hole and refuses other 3D objects, media and particles; denoise is not applied; only one geodesic camera is drawn. The tests ran on the NVIDIA adapter only; the software adapter and OpenGL were not run (the OpenGL case of the kind list returns early without a GL adapter). The films are not kept in the repository.

milestones.name: The ocean against the exact linear wave of a Gaussian hump
milestones.validation: Test ocean_reference (commit 166a7b3, 2026-10-06, release, load about 15, 15.8 s; deterministic): over water of 10 m at rest, g = 10 (c = 10 m/s), a Gaussian hump of sigma 8 m and amplitude 0.01 m (1e-3 of the depth), the linear shallow-water solution eta(r, t) = A integral_0^inf s exp(-s^2/2) J0(s r/sigma) cos(c s t/sigma) ds, evaluated in the test by Simpson's rule (1200 intervals on s in [0, 14]) with J0 by its integral representation (320 nodes) on a table of radii every 0.25 m read back by cubic interpolation (under 1e-5 of the amplitude); a closed basin of 160 x 160 m, dt 0.05, at t = 4 s (the front reaches the walls at 8 s); the exact crest is 0.1568 A at r = 44 m. Largest error of the surface over the cells as a fraction of A, by cells to sigma (4, 8, 16 and, in a disposable program, 32): first order 6.858e-2, 4.433e-2, 2.589e-2, 1.403e-2 (observed orders between consecutive rows 0.63, 0.78, 0.88; 0.70 over 4 to 16); second order 1.001e-2, 3.079e-3, 9.309e-4, 3.861e-4 (1.70, 1.73, 1.27; 1.71 over 4 to 16); the L2 error over A sigma in the disposable program was 0.510, 0.322, 0.185, 0.099 in first order and 0.067, 0.017, 0.0052, 0.0021 in second; the volume of the basin changes by at most 3.3e-14 (relative). milestones.limits: The solver is nonlinear and the reference linear: a hump of 1e-3 of the depth has a nonlinear correction of that order, which is where the second-order error stops falling (order 1.27 at 32 cells to sigma, 3.9e-4). One hump, one depth and one time: nothing about dispersion (the exact solution at finite depth is dispersive, and the solver is not), the depth response of the bed, the cavity of an entry or an open boundary. A test of what the solver already does: it passed when written and fails if the scheme loses its order. The wave of an impact has not been compared with any external reference; the SREP says so.

milestones.name: What dispersion does to the wave the shallow-water solver is compared with
milestones.validation: A disposable program (not in the repository; 2026-10-06, deterministic) evaluated the exact linear axisymmetric solution for a Gaussian hump of amplitude A on water of depth 10 m with g = 10: eta(r, t) = A integral_0^inf s exp(-s^2/2) F(s/sigma) J0(s r/sigma) cos(omega(s/sigma) t) ds, Simpson on s in [0, 14] with 2000 intervals and J0 by its integral representation (400 nodes), r scanned every 0.5 m; for the shallow-water wave omega = c k, c = 10 m/s and F = 1, for water of finite depth omega^2 = g k tanh(k h), and for a bed uplift F = 1/cosh(k h). Largest |eta|/A and where, shallow water against dispersive: sigma 40 m, t 20 s: 0.1568 at r = 220.5 m against 0.1516 at 214.5 m (leading crest 3 % lower, sigma/h = 4); sigma 16 m, t 8 s: crest 0.1568 at 88 m against a trough -0.1714 at 41.5 m (sigma/h = 1.6); sigma 8 m, t 4 s: crest 0.1568 at 44 m against a trough -0.2374 at 14 m, and t 8 s: 0.1148 at 84 m against -0.1366 at 42.5 m (sigma/h = 0.8); bed uplift (filtered) sigma 20 m, t 8 s: 0.1467 at 91 m against -0.1535 at 34 m, and sigma 8 m: 0.0625 at 85.5 m against -0.0741 at 43 m. The largest excursion is the criterion, not the leading crest, for the narrow humps: the dispersive trough trails the front and dominates it, so the comparison is a measure of how far the solver's wave is from the exact one and not of an error in a crest.
milestones.limits: A disposable program, so the figures are not in a test and cannot be rerun from the repository; the leading crest of the narrow humps was not isolated (only the largest excursion was recorded), so the only leading-crest figure is the 3 % at sigma/h = 4; the exact solution is linear (amplitude 1e-3 of the depth), the engine's cavity and its depth response are not in it. The references (Kajiura, Hammack, Kranzer and Keller, Cauchy and Poisson) were not read. The statement that the radius of the cavity of the authored rock is of the order of the depth is an estimate and not a measurement. No comparison with a measurement of a real impact exists.

milestones.name: What a crater that deforms costs the rigid world, and what was done about it
milestones.validation: Where the time goes (temporary timers in sr-sim physics3d.rs and sr-eval sim3d.rs, not in the repository; authored impact-land and impact-ocean scenes, ground of 160 x 160 segments = 25 921 vertices and 51 200 triangles, fixInternalEdges on, load1 about 10): in each rigid step that rebuilds the surface (5 a frame during the growth, 9 to 10 frames of each film), SharedShape::trimesh_with_flags 37.8 to 42.5 ms, the driver's surface 2.5 to 2.6 ms (crater growth 2.0, vertex map 0.5 to 0.6), set_shape 0.0 to 0.25 ms, the rapier step 1.5 ms; 3.0 s (land) and 1.9 s (ocean) of trimesh builds in 96 frames. Microbench of the build on that mesh: 15.9 ms without flags, 41.0 ms with FIX_INTERNAL_EDGES_TWO_SIDED; parry's TriMesh::set_vertices on a DEFORMABLE mesh 17.4 ms whatever number of vertices move. Step 1 (commit ce7f6d0): the law of an impact's crater was worked out at every rigid step after the crater had stopped growing (809 evaluations by 5 s of film, 303 of them by 2 s when the crater is whole); it is now worked out once per impact (test once_the_crater_has_stopped_growing_the_law_is_not_worked_out_again_for_every_rigid_step: 1 evaluation); median frame time between 2.5 and 4 s, three runs each at load1 18 to 23: land film 317, 376, 435 ms before and 235, 294, 296 ms after; ocean film 107, 108, 119 ms before and 55, 52, 54 ms after. Step 2 (commit a27753e): the shapes of the surfaces of a frame's rigid steps are built ahead on several threads once the impact is known, and each step takes the one whose vertices and triangles equal its own (test surface_prefetch: poses of 49 frames equal to the bit with and without, on 1, 2 and 8 threads and when replayed from a checkpoint; 54 steps took a shape built ahead); over the 15 frames of the contact (44 to 58) at load1 12 to 13, three runs each, without and with: ocean film 3.91, 3.65, 4.23 s and 2.07, 2.52, 2.45 s; land film 4.18, 4.32, 4.39 s and 3.89, 4.03, 3.74 s (on a shared machine at that load, so the parallel gain is smaller than the number of cores would give).
