The prefetch builds in parallel with the rayon pool, so its gain depends on the idle cores and is smaller on a busy one; a step in which an impact is noticed builds its shapes one by one, as before. The step cost is still the build of 40 ms on 5 cores, not under 3 ms: that needs a partial update of the touched facets, which parry does not offer (its pseudo-normals are read-only) and which would be a fork, left as a separate decision. The in-place trial changed one scene's poses by nothing, which proves nothing about other scenes; it was dropped for speed, not for a difference.

milestones.name: ocean@density: the density of the water
milestones.validation: `ocean@density` (positiveDecimal, default 1000, kg/m3) replaces the 1000 that the water had written into the group (the weight of what a body displaces and the force it is given back: group.rs), the momentum that the ejecta bring (divided by it: splash, particles3d.rs) and the target of the law of the cavity of an entry (cavity.rs, `Target::density`; the law's own table value for water is 1000.0 to the bit). The corpus has valid/ocean-density (buoyancy with density 1030) and invalid/ocean-density-zero (S06, the schema's range), and the corpus builder's oracle (xmllint) agrees with the loader on all 349 documents; before the attribute it reported 'Element ocean, attribute density: The attribute density is not allowed' for the valid one. Tests, all on the ci profile through the shared build queue: a ball of 2094 kg and 1 m radius floats within 0.03 m of the draft that its mass over the density needs in water of 1000, 1030 and 1100 kg/m3, higher in the denser water, by the difference of the drafts (ocean_buoyancy); density="1000" gives the heights of the document without the attribute to the bit (ocean_buoyancy); the ejecta of the crater of the impact scene bring, into water of 1030, momenta that times 1030 equal those into 1000 to 1e-9, the volume of solid is the same to 1e-12 and density="1000" is the default to the bit (ejecta_splash); the cavity in water of 1100 differs from that in 1000 by more than 1e-3 m in some cell and density="1000" is the default to the bit (water_entry); WaterAttrs reads 1000 without the attribute and 1030 with it (sr-eval lib). sr-eval lib 67, ejecta_splash 15, ocean_buoyancy 10, water_entry 7 pass; sr-model passes. The schema tests were written before the schema change and failed with the oracle's disagreement; the eval tests were written before the code read the attribute but were not run red (the first run was with the code in): a failing first run exists only for the schema and for the lib test of the defaults, which failed because the model fills the schema's default into the element (the attribute is never absent: the code reads 1000 from it).
milestones.limits: The momentum the solver exchanges is per unit of density and is not changed by it; what changes is where the density is multiplied back: in the force on a body (group.rs) and in the momentum of the ejecta. The weight of the water in the cavity's displaced volume is not modelled (the cavity is a displacement of volume). The attribute is one density for the whole ocean: no stratification, no salinity or temperature model. The test of the cavity asserts that the cavity changes with the density and not by how much: the law of the crater (cratering::crater) decides that and has its own tests. The gravity of the ocean and its density are independent attributes: a document can give both.

milestones.name: crater@mantle and crater@bulking: the crater keeps its volume and the ejecta come down as a mantle
milestones.validation: Before the attribute the ground of the authored rock (90 478 kg, 100 m/s at 60 degrees, soft rock: law volume V = 100.93 m3, rim crest radius 5.121 m, depth 2.794 m, ejecta 0.8 V = 80.74 m3) lost 0.959 V net and the ejecta were nowhere in it: the kernel's bump reaches the rim crest, so the bowl excavated 129.7 m3 (1.285 V) and the rim gave back 32.9 m3 (0.326 V). With `crater@mantle="true"` (only with `source`: CRT10) `sr_3d::crater::Crater::conserving` takes a Budget: the bowl bump is (1 - x^2)^p with p = pi R^2 d / V - 1, so it excavates exactly V with the law's depth and radius (p is clamped to 2 and the depth recomputed when p would be under 2); the mantle is t0 (R/r)^3 with t0 = 0.2899 m, brought in over the rim's width by a smooth ramp, cut at 20 crest radii and scaled by Simpson integration (20 000 intervals) to hold 0.8 V; the rim holds bulking x V - 0.8 V. `crater@bulking` (1 to 1.3, CRT10 and CRT11) is the ratio of what the rim and the mantle put back to V; its default, when it is absent, is what closes the law's own rim height with a 0.8 V mantle, 1.126 for the authored rock (0.326 V of rim and 0.8 V of mantle), derived from the law and not chosen; 1 gives a rim of 0.2 V. Tests in sr-3d geometry: with the default, with 1 and with 1.3 the net volume of the change of height equals (bulking - 1) V to 1e-6 of V (measured: bowl 100.928, rim 32.865 / 20.186 / 50.464, mantle 80.742 m3); the mantle falls as the inverse cube outside the rim and stops at 20 crest radii; the depth and the radius of the law are kept and the map keeps its orientation; a budget that cannot be met (V = 400) is an error. In sr-eval (scene units, pixels a metre 1) the ground the crater moves adds up to the law's volume with the mantle (bowl 2.736, rim 0.891, mantle 2.189 against V = 2.733) and without it is as it was (bowl 3.515, rim 0.891, mantle 0). The ejecta that come to rest on the ground are removed so that they are not counted twice: `particles3d::Spec::settle` is a rest speed, set by the evaluator to 0.5 m/s when a burst's crater has a mantle; a particle whose speed relative to the surface after a contact is under it is removed where it lies and told to the driver as `Absorbed { ground: true }`, which the splash aggregator ignores, so only water takes from the ocean. Tests in sr-sim particles_settle (settle at the first impact of a 4.95 m/s rebound with a rest speed of 6; at the fourth impact, 0.62 m/s, with 1; with none nothing is taken and a replay with a small checkpoint tells the same lists) and in sr-eval crater_ejecta_ground (1000 ejecta at 5.5 s without the mantle and 621 with it, 88 at 1.6 s in both; one of the 621 slow and within 1 cm of the ground; scrubbing gives the same frame). The corpus has 4 invalid and 2 valid documents for the two attributes and the oracle agrees with the loader on all 355. Without the attribute the bits are as they were. Commits fdff08e, ac90f74 and 9f32bb8 (2026-10-06) and the one that adds the settle. The tests of the budget and of the evaluator were written before the code but not run red; the settle tests were written first and did not compile before the field existed, and the first run of the eval test failed because the evaluator read the attribute from the wrong element.
milestones.limits: The transient stage of the crater, its collapse into the final one, is not modelled: the law's radius is the final, apparent radius and a transient radius 1.2 to 1.3 larger would count the collapse twice. The mantle is analytic: t0 (R/r)^3 is the McGetchin et al. 1973 and Collins et al. 2005 form, with a cut at 20 crest radii that is a choice, and it is not the footprint of the particles' landing points (that comparison is a separate measurement, not made yet). Bulking is one number for the whole crater: no dependence on distance, porosity or compaction of the target. The bulking that closes the law follows from 0.326 V for the law's rim height and the 0.8 share, both constants of the law (RIM_HEIGHT 0.036 of the rim diameter, EJECTA_SHARE 0.8), not fitted here. The mantle is part of the ground only: where the crater is in water the sea sweeps change with the mantle under the water, and those tests assert order, not a number; the sea table is to be redone. The rest speed of 0.5 m/s is a choice, not a measurement; a particle that is slow at the top of a hop near the ground without having touched it stays. A removed particle's mass is not tracked: the volume of the mantle is the law's 0.8 V whatever the particles' own number and masses (the burst's particles stand for the ejecta and do not conserve its volume). Removed particles give their momentum and energy to nothing.

milestones.name: The ejecta's landing points against the analytic mantle (a measurement)
milestones.validation: The test the_ballistic_landing_points_of_the_ejecta_make_a_mantle_that_is_measured_against_the_inverse_cube launches 20 000 ejecta of the authored rock (90 478 kg of 2700 kg/m3, 100 m/s at 60 degrees, soft rock, law crest radius 6.658 m) with the engine's ejecta model, lets them fall on level ground at g = 9.80665 with no drag (closed-form range 2 vh vy / g) and bins the landing mass by radius. Printed on 2026-10-06 for launch angle and spread 45/15, 30/10 and 60/10 degrees: the share of the mass that lands inside the crest radius is 0.8403, 0.8612, 0.8608; between 1 and 20 crest radii 0.1598, 0.1388, 0.1392; beyond 20 radii none (the farthest bins are about 3.5 crest radii). Log-log slope of the thickness (mass over annulus area) in 12 bins from 1 to 20 crest radii, over the bins that hold mass: -6.95, -4.07, -4.22, against -3 for the mantle. Of the mass that lands outside the crest, 83 to 89 % lies in 1 to 2 crest radii, against 52.6 % for t0 (R/r)^3. It asserts only that the shares add up to 1 and the slope is finite: it is a measurement, not a requirement.
milestones.limits: Level, undeformed ground (the particles in the scene land on the growing crater, its rim and the mantle itself), no drag, no bounce or rolling, and landing points only (the removal of settled ejecta in the scene is by rest speed, not by landing). The launch model is the engine's own (Housen and Holsapple scaling as the engine reads it), whose launch radii span the crater: the 84 to 86 percent that land inside the crest are mass that falls back into the bowl, which the apparent crater of the law already has netted out and the kernel's bowl does not model. The result is for one rock and one material; the slope depends on the bin edges and on how few bins hold mass (5, 4 and 4). It does not show that the inverse cube is wrong: it shows that these particles do not reproduce it, so the mantle of the ground is the law's statement and not the particles' landing.

milestones.name: Granular bed: a height field of deposit that relaxes to the angle of repose
milestones.validation: sr_sim::granular::Bed is a height field of deposit over a ground on a square grid. deposit() shares a volume among the four nearest cells by bilinear weights; relax() passes over the cells in row-major order and each cell with deposit gives half the excess of its surface over tan(theta) x distance to each lower neighbour among sixteen (the eight around it and the eight a knight's move away), as much as it holds, until no transfer in a pass exceeds the tolerance. Tests in tests/granular: the oracle of the cone (a volume V = pi r^3 tan(theta) / 3 poured in 30 equal pours at the middle of level ground, relaxing after each; r = 10 cells, theta = 35 degrees): volume kept to +8.9e-16 (oracle 1e-9), flank angle in each of 24 sectors of 15 degrees, from the least-squares slope between 0.3 and 0.7 of the radius, 34.13 to 35.59 degrees (axis 35.00, diagonal 34.64; oracle 2 degrees), base radius 10.44 cells against 10. Other angles and sizes: 25 degrees at 12 cells 23.72 to 25.45, 40 at 12 cells 38.33 to 40.57, 35 at 20 cells 34.52 to 35.60, 30 at 10 cells 29.16 to 30.49 (all within 2 degrees); 30 at 8 cells 26.89 to 30.80 and 30 at 5 cells 26.15 to 30.00 (not within 2). Volume kept to 4e-15 or better in all. The same pours twice give equal beds, to the bit. A layer 0.5 thick on a ramp of 30 degrees (under the angle) takes no pass and is unchanged; on 40 degrees it runs to the foot in 590 passes, the volume kept to the bit, no cell negative, the first and last row of the 8 differ by 1.0e-3 of a deposit 2.29 high (the order of the passes). The prototype with 4, 8 and 16 neighbours (python, Jacobi relaxation, pile of 10 cells, 35 degrees): flank 38.89 to 44.48, 35.07 to 36.85 and 35.06 to 35.49 degrees; the implementation measures 34.13 to 35.59 with sixteen and sequential relaxation, and the other stencils were not built in it. The tests were written before the code and did not compile before it existed; they were not run red.
milestones.limits: It is connected to the scene by crater@repose (the next milestone); the numbers above are of the module as first built, and the active-box version used there differs from them by 0.01 degrees at most. The angle of the pile is within 2 degrees only from ten cells of radius up: a pile of fewer cells than that has the discretisation's angle, not the declared one, and a pile that small is not resolved by the grid. The angle is one number for the whole bed (no cohesion, no different static and dynamic angles, no grains' size); a height field holds no overhang and does not flow under a body; relaxation is quasi-static: it has no time, so a pile reaches its angle at once, and the flow of an avalanche is not modelled. The sequential order of passes leaves an asymmetry: 1.0e-3 between mirror rows on the ramp (0.04 percent of the heap). The edge of the grid holds the material in. Cost: the cone of 10 cells' radius takes tenths of a second for 30 relaxations on a 49 by 49 grid; a grid the size of a crater scene (hundreds of cells to a side) has not been measured.

milestones.name: crater@repose: the ejecta that settle make a deposit on the ground
milestones.validation: `crater@repose` (xs:double, 10 to 60, degrees; only with `source`: CRT10; not with `mantle="true"`: CRT12, because the settled ejecta would be the ground twice) makes the emitter of the crater's ejecta take out each particle that comes to rest on the ground (rest speed 0.5 m/s, Spec::settle, as with the mantle) and tell the log of what settled (splash::Log, a second ExchangeLog next to the ocean's, compared to the bit on a replay) where it lay in the plane of the crater and the volume of the target it stood for (mass over the target's density, in the owner's object units cubed). debris::State pours those volumes step by step onto an sr_sim::granular::Bed of 144 by 144 cells (12 to the crest radius, 6 crest radii to each side) over the grown crater (its rise is the ground the pile relaxes on), relaxing after each step, keeps the bed after each step it folded and at checkpoints (every 8 steps, thinned to 128), and the bed after the steps the frame's particles computed is sr_3d::crater::Deposit added in the kernel's map (height and jacobian) to the crater of the frame node that the render and whatever runs after the particles read. Tests: sr-3d (the integral of the rise equals the deposit's volume, 8.828087 against 8.828101; the rise at points equals the deposit's height to 1e-12; the jacobian matches finite differences and keeps its orientation; an empty deposit gives the bits of the crater without one); sr-eval crater_ejecta_ground (written first, failed with no deposit; then: 1000 ejecta of the authored rock, thrown 169 634.1 kg, 96 012.9 kg still moving at 5.5 s, 73 621.2 kg settled, deposit 35.057715 m3 against 35.057715 for the settled mass over 2100 kg/m3, to 1e-9; none at 1.6 s and none without the attribute; the volume at 2, 3, 4 and 5.5 s is 0, 9.451, 9.774, 35.058; going back and forward and a fresh evaluator give the same deposit, equal to the bit; four frames take 2.08 s with it and 2.24 s without, within the noise). Corpus: 4 documents more (359), the oracle agrees. Commits on feat/granular-bed.
milestones.limits: The particles and the rigid world land on the ground without the deposit (so a particle settles on the crater as it is and the deposit is added above it), and what reads the crater after the particles in a frame sees it, which includes the render and any simulation that runs later (an ocean's bed or a smoke's colliders would see the deposit under them; neither was tested with it). The ground the deposit relaxes on is the final crater, also for ejecta that settle while it grows (few do before about 0.6 s). What settles beyond 6 crest radii is put on the edge of the bed (for the authored rock the ejecta of the engine's model reach about 3.5). An emitter deposits on one crater; with several that have a repose angle the scene is an error. The deposit is bilinear between cell centres: its normals are not continuous across cells. A deposit of heights over the crater's influence depth would bend the map; the map refuses what makes it fold over and the frame fails with the error. It does not move with an owner that moves except through the owner's pose (the plane coordinates are taken at the end of each step). The cost was measured once, on one scene, with the machine loaded by others; the whole relaxation after each step is of the cells that ever held deposit. The sea sweeps and the render were not run with it; the GPU renderer reads the deposit through the same crater deformation as the mantle but a render with it was not checked.

milestones.name: Voxel physics: the occupancy of a voxel object and its rigid body (P1 and P2)
milestones.validation: P1: sr_3d::occupancy::Occupancy is a sparse grid of cells with a palette index (0 empty) in bricks of 8x8x8 with a revision that changes only when a cell does, the bricks changed since a revision (emptied ones included until compact), a content fingerprint equal for equal content in any order and history, an optional brick limit, and the scan order z, y, x. Moments are exact integer sums (i128) of the doubled coordinates, so mass, centre and inertia come from one division each and are the same bits in any order of the cells (tested with 4 shuffles); a box of 4x3x5 cells of 0.5x0.25x0.2 m has the closed-form mass, centre and inertia to 1e-12 with exactly zero products; an L of three cells matches the hand-worked values (m 3, centre (5/6, 5/6, 1/2), Ixx = Iyy = 7/6, Izz = 11/6, Ixy = 1/3) to 1e-15; the principal axes (cyclic Jacobi in a fixed order) rebuild the tensor to 1e-13 and are right-handed. components() labels by face connectivity in scan order: face 1, edge 2, corner 2, a ring 1, cut once 1, cut twice 2, a sealed shell 1, a diagonal of 9 cells 9, across brick borders and the origin 1; independent of input order and duplicates. P2: Shape3::Voxels { size, cells } is a Rapier voxel collider (the scene's half turn about x maps a cell [i, j, k] to [i, -j-1, -k-1], so no cell is moved by half a cell); its mass properties equal the exact integer ones to 1e-12 (mass, centre and all of the tensor, in scene axes, at two scales of the scene; test in sr-eval voxels). Rest oracle: a block of 6x4x6 cells (0.5x0.25x0.5 m) dropped on the floor rests at the same height as the box of the same size and mass: difference 8.6e-7 m at 1/60 s and 2.0e-8 m at 1/240 s (oracle 1e-6; the margin at 1/60 s is small); both tilt the same (3.7e-5 rad at 1/240 s, the solver's). A stack of three 8x8x8-cell blocks (2 m) dropped with gaps stands for 8 s like the stack of boxes: the largest difference of a coordinate from the boxes' is 2.4 mm at 1/60 s and 1.2e-5 m at 1/120 s, the top at the same height to 0.1 mm. Cost (examples/voxel_probe, ci profile, 8 cores shared with others at a load of about 8): build of the world 2.3 ms for a floor of 1e4 cells, 18 ms for 1e5, 166 ms for 1e6 (about 170 ns a cell); a block of 4096 cells falling on those floors takes 0.013, 0.061 and 0.54 ms a step (a box floor: 0.012 ms with a still block, 0.2 ms tumbling), a block of 64 000 cells 0.15 to 0.7 ms on 1e4-1e5 cells, 250 000 cells 2.0 to 2.6 ms on a floor of 1e5 to 1e6 cells; a body at rest is put to sleep and costs 0.001 to 0.1 ms; the checkpoints hold 0.18 to 0.40 MB whatever the cells (the shape is shared between a checkpoint and the world, which an edit of the cells would break: see the limits). The cache key of a world hashes the cells (physcache). The workspace builds with the new variant; hydrostatics refuses a body of cells. Edit cost (examples/voxel_edit_probe, same machine and load, one run): removing cells from a Rapier voxel collider while a copy (a checkpoint) still holds the shape costs the copy of the shape plus the edits: 1 cell from 1e4 cells 0.012 ms, from 1e5 cells 0.12 ms, from 1e6 cells 0.94 ms; 1 000 cells from 1e6 cells 0.82 ms; 100 000 cells from 1e6 cells 7.2 ms (6.5 ms for the same number of edits on a shape nobody else holds); a private copy of 1e6 cells is 1.8 MiB resident (264 KiB for 1e5, too small to see for 1e4). So the removal of a crater's cells is a few milliseconds even at 1e6 cells, and the memory of a retained checkpoint after an edit is about 1.8 bytes a cell. Bulk construction for an importer: Occupancy::from_bricks and from_cells (any order, duplicate cells and bricks and index 0 are errors, a limit on bricks) have the fingerprint of the same cells set one by one, with every brick new to a reader at revision 0; the 256-entry RGBA palette beside the cells does not change the cells' revision or fingerprint when recoloured, and has its own revision and an appearance fingerprint. CORRECTION (2026-10-07, found while writing the test of a voxel body fractured into voxel fragments, by comparing Rapier with the exact integer moments over every proportion of box): the sentence above that Rapier's mass properties of the cells equal the exact integer ones to 1e-12 is FALSE in general. It held for the asymmetric body that was tested and for boxes whose largest moment is not on x, but for a tensor that is diagonal with two equal moments and the third larger on x (a plate thin along x, a block shorter along x than it is wide) Parry's eigen solver returned principal values and a frame that do not belong together: a block of 3 by 4 by 4 cells had 234.4 about x where the exact value is 300, and a 1 by 7 by 7 plate with a hole had 478 against 937. It was not only the helper: the world simulated those bodies with that tensor (a plate spun up at 0.0836 rad/s2 under a torque that, with its cells' inertia, gives 0.0427). My earlier checks compared Rapier with Rapier (shape_mass_properties was built on the same Parry call), which is why they agreed. Fixed in a new commit: sr_sim::physics3d::voxel_mass computes the tensor from the cells with exact i128 sums, diagonalises it by Jacobi rotations that leave a diagonal tensor alone, and gives Rapier the principal moments and frame explicitly (the collider of a body of cells, the pieces and the part that stays after a cut, and shape_mass_properties use it; the source of a fracture whose fragments are bodies of cells has the exact sum of theirs, sum_mass_properties, because Parry's Sum goes through the same solver and gave a source of 3 by 4 by 4 cells, fractured into two halves along z, an Ixx of 234.4 instead of 300 until it fractured, which Urano's review found and a test now covers; fractures of other shapes still use Parry's Sum, unchanged). Tests that failed first: sr-eval mass_properties (17 box proportions at three places with cubic cells and with cells of three sizes, 40 random sets, a cross, a plate with a hole, a hollow box: every entry of the tensor to 1e-12 against sr_3d::occupancy::Moments) and sr-eval world_inertia (the world's spin-up under a torque against the exact I^-1 tau, for five shapes and four torques, and for a plate and the block that stays after a cut). The rest-height and stack tests of this entry are not affected by the inertia (they held before and after).
milestones.limits: [AS OF THAT COMMIT; later entries of this ledger supersede it: P3 to P6 have since been built in part (slots and splitting, the pure crater, the world side of fracture), the mass properties are no longer Parry's, and the checkpoint figures count voxel shapes by their cells] P3 to P6 are not built: no fragments, no removal by a crater, no fracture partition, no sequences or revision cache, no schema (rigidBody@shape=voxels, density, maxFragments and the rest are approved names and not in the schema yet), no eval path from an Occupancy to a body, and no rule. The rest oracle holds to 1e-6 m at 1/60 s by a margin of 14 percent; it measures that the cells and the box agree, not that either is right (both rest 6.9e-5 m into the floor: Rapier's allowed penetration). The stack differs from the box stack by millimetres at 1/60 s: the solver is sensitive to a contact made of many points against four. Jitter at rest could not be measured because bodies fall asleep; a body kept awake (a moving floor, an applied force) was not probed. The step costs are from one run on a loaded machine and from falling and tumbling blocks of one shape, not from a scene; a voxel body on the 51k-triangle crater mesh and the cost of a body that is moving for a long time at 1e6 cells were not measured. The checkpoint figures are the world's own estimate (the shape is shared by reference, so they do not count it): an edit of the cells (P3, P4) copies the whole shape if a checkpoint still holds it, so P3 has to charge the edited shapes to the checkpoint budget (about 1.8 KiB per thousand cells, measured below). Voxels refuse buoyancy (the displaced volume is not a mesh). Keys must stay within 2^20 of the origin and 2^32 cells for the moments to fit i128.

milestones.name: Voxel physics: slots and the splitting of a body of cells (P3)
milestones.validation: World3::with_voxel_splits registers bodies of cells (the parents) and the dynamic placeholder bodies of cells that the pieces take (the slots, `maxFragments` of them, disabled until used, in the world from its build as the fracture pieces are, so the body count never changes and a replay from a checkpoint is the same). Driver3::voxel_cut(t, parent, installed revision, impact) is a pure function of its arguments that says what the body has lost: the destroyed cells, the mass of what stays, and the pieces (cells and mass); the world checks all of it before changing anything (a cell the body has not, a mass that is not positive, more pieces than free slots are errors that leave the world as it was; the shape is edited on a private copy), then installs it at the start of the step: the parent loses the destroyed cells and the pieces' cells, takes the new mass and keeps the velocity of its new centre of mass, v + w x (c_new - c_old); each piece takes the next free slot with the parent's pose and spin and the velocity of the point of the body its centre of mass was, v + w x (c_i - c_old). Rapier's own mass properties of the cells are used (they equal the exact integer ones, P2). Tests (written first, red = did not compile): bar of 12x2x2 cells of 0.25 m spinning (20, 10, 40 deg/s) and moving, cut at 0.5 s: a slice of 4 cells destroyed, the part of 20 cells stays and the part of 24 cells is the piece: before the cut the slots do not take part (enabled = [true, false, false]), after it the piece starts with the parent's pose to the bit, its velocity equals v + w x (c - c_old) to 1e-12 and its spin the body's, the remaining part's velocity is that of its own centre of mass to 1e-12, and the momentum of the remaining part, the piece and the destroyed slice (at the rigid velocity it had) equals the bar's to 2e-12 of its mass; the cut is installed once; two pieces take the slots in order and one slot for two pieces is an error that says slot; [CORRECTED after the independent review, see the end of this entry: the replay claim first made here was hollow] a body of cells is charged to the checkpoints by its cells (about 2 bytes a cell, as a mesh is by its triangles: 100 704 bytes for 400 cells and 242 304 for 24 000 in four checkpoints, the difference at least 2 bytes x 23 600 cells x 3); registration refuses a parent that is not made of cells and a slot that is not a dynamic body of cells of the parent's size. In sr-eval, pure functions (not wired to any attribute): body(occupancy, cell size, density, ppm) is the shape (the cells in scan order) and the mass N x density x cell volume; cut(before, destroyed, revision, ..., policy, anchor) divides what is left by connected components: which part stays (the largest, the first of equals, or every part that touches an anchor), which parts below `min_cells` are dust, which become pieces in scan order, and, over `max_fragments`, an error or the smallest become dust; tests check that every cell is in exactly one part (destroyed, piece, stays), that masses add up to 1e-12 (24+20 cells of 48 with 4 destroyed), that the result is the same for the cells put in in another order, that a tie is broken by position, that cells that are not in the body are ignored, and the anchored case (a slab held by its bottom row: two held halves stay and nothing is loose; a cut that frees a block of 12 cells makes one piece). Occupancy also has bounds(), extent(), Limits on bricks, cells and bytes that error instead of truncating, and estimate_bytes (for the importer: refuse a model from its header). INDEPENDENT REVIEW (2026-10-07, five reviewers by dimension and two skeptics for each finding, 53 agents: 24 findings, 18 confirmed by both skeptics, 3 disputed, 3 refuted). What it found in this work and what was done, each with a test that failed first: (1) frame_at's closing sequence applied the colliders, visibility and fractures of the instant asked for but not the voxel cuts, which step_once applies before it records its frame, so the frame at the step of a cut was the uncut one from a fresh request and the cut one from the log of a later request: the same time gave different bits depending on the history of the questions (what I had explained, wrongly, as 'a frame shows a cut only once the world is asked past it'). Fixed (the tail applies the cuts, idempotently); the invariant test asks each of the 12 steps around a cut at 1.5 s from a fresh world, from a world asked later and then again, and from a world that keeps no frames and replays from a checkpoint, and all are equal to the bit. (2) The replay tests of the first version were hollow: they asked later times first, so every frame came from the frame log, and their checkpoint budgets of 4 000 and 6 000 bytes admit no checkpoint, so nothing was replayed; the claim in this entry that frames asked in an order from worlds with no checkpoint, 4 kB or the default are equal to the bit was therefore not supported. World3::checkpoint_restores now counts the times the world was taken back to a checkpoint, the replay tests keep no frames and assert at least one restore for each step back in time (and, with the default budget, that checkpoints other than the first were taken), and the second-cut and slot-as-parent tests replay in the same way. P1 and P2 made no claim of replay (their ledger entry speaks of the rest of a block, a stack, the cost and the checkpoint charge only), so nothing in them was hollow in that way. (3) A cut that left parent_mass 0 disabled the parent once and the next step's visibility sync switched it on again with its emptied collider: State records it as spent. (4) The cuts of one call were installed one split after another, so a failure of the second left the first installed: all are asked for and checked before any is applied (a body that becomes a slot in use in a call is cut from the next step). (5) Registration refuses two splits of one body, a ring of splits and a fracture's source or piece as a parent. (6) The mass and inertia that the world installs are now observed: pushed with a force and a torque, the part that stays and the piece accelerate as F/m to 1e-9 and spin up as I^-1 tau to 2e-3 with those of their cells, also for a piece whose slot is hidden when it is cut (the reviewers' claim that Rapier skips the recompute while the slot is disabled does not show: that test passes before and after); the slot-order test observes the centre of mass of each slot (and fails when the pieces are swapped, checked by mutation); a second cut as the difference from the first and a slot as the parent of another split are tested, and a third cut with no free slot is an error; in sr-eval ties are tested with six shuffles of the input and the full tensor at the second scale. Occupancy: keys outside [-2^30, 2^30) are refused (components() panicked at i32::MAX and a brick key of 2^28 could be stored but not named), estimate_bytes saturates (it wrapped to 0 for a box as wide as the keys), a brick key given twice is an error even if the second copy is empty, palette index 0 has no colour to set. Refuted or left: the revision doc was loosened to say a revision compares states of one grid only. LATER CORRECTION: the mass/inertia observation test of the review round compared the world with shape_mass_properties, which was built on the same Parry call as the world, so it could not see the inertia defect described in the entry of P2; the independent test (sr-eval world_inertia, against the exact integer moments) replaced it in value, and the fix is a new commit. SECOND REVIEW (Urano, of 7df5118): (a) the tail of frame_at does not record its frame, so asking the same time twice re-ran apply_voxel_cuts on a state the tail had already changed, and with chained splits {0 -> [1, 2]}, {1 -> [3]} and the child's cut scripted at the parent's step the first request gave enabled [T, T, F, T] and the second [T, T, F, F]: State now remembers the step at which each slot was taken into use, and a slot is cut from the step after; the invariant test is a helper over any world and driver (plain case and chained case; fresh, asked four times, asked later, replayed from a checkpoint). (b) the mass/inertia observation test now includes a piece that is an L (products of inertia) so that a swapped or rotated axis shows, which the symmetric pieces could not; the replay tests of the second cut and of the slot as parent now also assert that checkpoints beyond the first were taken. THIRD ROUND: the cuts of a step are applied before its loads (a load that reads the body found the pre-cut body when the step was reached by stepping straight through and the post-cut body after a frame had been asked for at that instant: red test with a load that depends on the centre of mass, through the four ways).
milestones.limits: No scene uses it: no attribute (rigidBody@shape=voxels and the rest wait for the schema), no impact that triggers a cut (P4: crater@source on a body of cells), no ejecta from the destroyed cells, no fracture partition (P5), no sequences or revision cache (P6). The driver's cut is relative to the installed revision: a second cut has to be the difference from the first (tested). A slot may be the parent of another split once it is in use (tested); within one call a body that becomes a slot in use is cut from the next step. Joints of the parent stay with the parent. A piece starts touching its parent along the edges or corners where components meet (they share no face), so the first step resolves those contacts: not measured. Dust is not given any motion here (P4 turns the cells of `destroyed` and the dust into particles). The charge of voxel shapes to the checkpoints counts the cells in full for every checkpoint, as meshes are, which is conservative: a world of a 1e6-cell floor loses about 2 MB of checkpoint budget per checkpoint, and about 14 MB when the floor is a registered parent [MESH FRACTURE, changed by the same review: the source of every fracture (mesh or cells) now has the exact sum of its pieces' tensors, and the pieces of a mesh fracture have tensors worked out exactly from their triangles, because Parry's MassProperties::sum and from_trimesh diagonalise with the solver whose mistake the voxel code works around (a diagonal tensor with a repeated smallest moment and the larger on x reads back with its axes swapped); the pieces' tensors and the source's change in the low bits and no golden hash moved; impact-block is the only example with a fracture and no hero or pipeline scene has one; tests mesh_fracture_inertia and voxel_fracture] [CORRECTED after the second review: the state also keeps the cells of every body that can be cut, twelve bytes a cell and a new copy for every cut, which the charge first left out; checkpoint_charge counts them, and the test a_registered_parent_is_charged_to_the_checkpoints_for_the_cells_the_state_keeps_of_it_too fails on the old charge (the checkpoints grew by 141 600 bytes for 23 600 more cells, where 14 bytes a cell in the checkpoints taken needs 991 200)] (counting the cells costs a pass over the shape each time a checkpoint is saved: not measured). A parent whose cut leaves nothing is disabled and its pieces take slots. Axes: the cells of a cut are keys in the parent's own frame, which are the scene's.

milestones.name: Voxel physics: a crater in ground made of cells, the pure part (P4)
milestones.validation: sr_eval::voxel_crater::excavate(occupancy, crater kernel, cell size in metres, ejection) takes the law's crater out of ground made of cells and says what is thrown and what is heaped on the rim, in counts of cells. The kernel is the conserving one with a bulking of 1 (its bowl holds the law's volume and its rim the 0.2 that is not thrown); sr-eval's ground_kernel (Crater::new, exponent 2, no budget) is NOT that kernel and holds 129.7 m3 for the same crater, so the wiring of a voxel owner has to build the conserving kernel with bulking 1: this is stated in the module and is the wiring's to do. REMOVAL (second design, after the pre-review of aeb7b39 by Urano): a filled cell goes when its centre is within the crest radius plus the rim's width, over the kernel's own grown surface S(r) = rim_height_at(r) - bowl_depth_at(r) (the accessors are checked against Crater::map at points of the original ground to 1e-12, twice: for a kernel with no mantle, and for the kernel the evaluator builds, which has one, where the mantle's height (new accessor mantle_height_at, half its thickness at the crest) is a third term; the voxel crater follows the bowl and the rim and NOT the mantle, because the ejecta are particles there that settle as cells, so its lip matches the rendered surface of the analytic kernel only up to the mantle), and under one crest radius above the crater's plane; the set equals that of a brute force over the whole ground. For the authored rock (law volume 100.928 m3, crest radius 6.658 m, depth 2.794 m) in a slab of 0.25 m cells with a 15 m pillar of 2x2 cells near the axis: 6 460 cells, 100.9375 m3, within a cell of the law's (100.9275 m3 is 6 459.36 cells) ONLY because the pillar's cells over the plane (108 of them) make up for the wall that the lip stands on: on flat ground alone the crater takes out 6 352 cells, 99.25 m3, 98.34 percent of the law's, which is the figure for the crater as such, numbers pinned from the run; the part of the pillar inside the reach of the crater goes and what stands higher than one crest radius over the plane stays. BUDGET IN CELLS: thrown = round(0.8 N) = 5 168, uplift 1 292, rim 1 292; every removed cell is thrown or uplifted once; the palette histogram of the ground after (less the removed, plus the rim with the palette of the uplifted cells) plus the thrown equals that before. THE RIM is the law's: the level of a cell is its height over the floor of the bowl in units of the height of the rim at its distance from the axis, and the rim is the first 1 292 cells that are held up (the face-neighbour under each, along minus the axis, is ground or another cell of the rim) in order of level: the surface of the law's rim scaled by 1.2743, on both sides of the crest radius (between a quarter and three quarters of the cells are inside it). Checked: every rim cell is empty before, not taken out, held up from below, at or under the level; and a brute force over the box finds no cell that is under the level and held up and not in the rim. SPEEDS: cells ordered by distance from the axis, then the highest first (the law launches the shallowest fastest: the Z-model of Maxwell), then the scan; they take the engine's launch model's distribution by quantiles of mass (cell i of T has the speed above which the fraction (i + 1/2) / T of the law's mass lies); the order is checked cell pair by cell pair (distance does not fall, at one distance the shallower first, speed does not rise), the share of cells faster than the speed at the law's 0.05, 0.2, 0.5, 0.8 and 0.95 mass fractions matches within 0.01 + 2/T, the fastest cell has the law's fastest speed to 5 percent, directions are along the radius out of the cell with an elevation in 45 +- 15 degrees, and the result is the same for the cells put in in reverse order. Mutation checks: ordering the cells of one distance by depth the other way, and ranking the rim by distance from the level 1, each make a test fail. ERRORS: no ground, nothing taken; share 1, no rim; share 0.4, rim 60 percent with a level over 1; share 0 asks the rim for the whole bowl, which it has not the room for (region up to level 4), an error that says so; a kernel in the scene's units over cells in metres (crest radius 2 663 cells) is refused with the reason; a centre out of the range of the keys is refused (index arithmetic is in i64, no saturating casts). UNITS: excavate takes the unit of the kernel's lengths in metres and reads the kernel in metres (a kernel in half-metres declared as 0.5 gives the same removed, rim and uplift to the bit; one in the scene's units declared as 0.01 gives the same crater within 8 cells); the box that is scanned has a cap of 2^27 cells that errors at once with the reason (the earlier refusal was a threshold on the crest radius in cells, which a scene-unit kernel over 0.25 m cells with a 4 m crest, 1 600 cells, passed before hanging in a scan of billions of cells). The crest radius that the test of the wrong units uses is 2 660 cells (665 / 0.25). crater_cut(before, kernel, kernel unit, ejection, revision, Rock{size, density, pixels_per_meter, policy}, anchored) is the pure glue for the world: it excavates, makes the ground with the rim on it, divides what is left as voxels::cut does (the rim joins before anything leaves, so a loose part of the rim goes with its piece) and returns the cut with `added` = the rim's cells (VoxelCut3::added, heaped before anything leaves: a cell the body has or named twice is refused and installs nothing). Tests: the 6460-cell crater gives 1292 added cells none of which was ground, and every cell of ground and rim is destroyed, staying or in a piece exactly once, every kilogram once; given to a world of 576 000 cells the body has the centre of mass of the cells that stay to 1e-6 m and the piece takes its slot; a ball dropped on a floor of cells that a cut heaped half a metre on rests at 0.8 m and not 0.3 m (red without the heaping); a crater cut of the same arguments is the same value, and cells that are not cubes, a kernel unit of 0 and ground with no cells are errors.
milestones.limits: The speeds are the engine's launch model's distribution, not something the cells give: the cells carry the mass, the place and the palette. Which removed cells are thrown (the middle, the shallowest) and which are uplifted (the wall) is a choice made here, not the law's. The rim holds at most what its region up to level 4 allows: a share thrown under about 20 percent is an error. The removal takes everything inside the crest radius plus the rim's width over the surface up to one crest radius over the plane, so a hill in the crater's footprint goes with the bowl. The crater is in the frame of the cells in metres: the owner's scale, the cell size in object units and pixels per metre are the caller's to bring to it (a crest radius over 2 000 cells is refused as being in other units), and were not tested together. 'Held up' is the face-neighbour most nearly against the axis: for an axis that is not a lattice axis this is an approximation, and the tests have the axis along a lattice axis and a flat ground. The cost of the rim's region (a pass over a box of about 76 cubed cells) was not measured. The thrown cells are not yet particles, and what the cut of the remaining ground makes of the loose parts has now been put through the world once with this removal (crater_cut, below: the law's crater in the 30 m slab with its pillar, 1292 cells heaped, 6460 destroyed, the top of the pillar, 132 cells, a piece), not with a crater that is thrown at a body by a scene. Slanted axes: tests have the axis along a lattice axis, at 45 degrees in the x-y plane on flat ground (a wide crater of 12 m with 480 000 cells, whose first reach missed 64 440 cells and is now the hypotenuse of the crest and the rim) and no ground that slopes or axis out of that plane: those are untested. The first design of the rim (nearest the crest first) made a flat-topped ring and did not follow the law's surface; it was replaced after the pre-review.

milestones.name: Voxel physics: a body of cells fractured into bodies of cells (the world side of P5)
milestones.validation: The world's existing fracture (World3::with_fractures, pieces that are bodies from the start and are enabled at the event) takes bodies of cells as pieces: a block of 8 by 4 by 4 cells with a spin of (20, 10, 40) deg/s and a velocity, fractured at t = 0 into three pieces of unequal shape (an end of 3 columns, a step of half height, the rest), each piece has the spin of the body and the velocity of the point of the body its centre of mass was to 1e-12, and the linear momentum (to 1e-12 of the mass) and the angular momentum about the centre of the whole (to 1e-12) are those of the block. This test failed first (angular momentum 256.3 against 279.3) and is what exposed the inertia defect of Parry's voxel mass properties (see the entry of P2). The angular-momentum check of this test is, given the inertias that the world holds, an identity of the parallel-axis theorem (a review remark): the independent evidence that the world holds the right inertias is sr-eval world_inertia (the spin-up of a source and of pieces against the exact moments, including a source of 3 by 4 by 4 cells fractured later into two halves along z, which failed before the exact sum), so this test is the kinematic rule (spin and velocity of each piece) and the conservation given those.
milestones.limits: Only the world side: the partition of an occupancy into pieces (PieceGraph, agreed with Saturno) and the eval wiring of fracture@source on a voxel owner are not built; the fracture at t = 0 and without radial impulse or contact was tested, not a fracture on an impact. Registration of fractures and splits excludes the same body in both orders (tested).

milestones.name: pyro@follow: the window of an open smoke domain follows its plume, and what that did to the hero scene
milestones.validation: pyro@follow, followMargin and followLoss (PYRO9 to PYRO11) move the window of an open domain, in whole cells, to keep the smoke followMargin cells from the faces it is going toward; the number of cells, and so the memory and the cost of a step, do not change (the decision is 2.2 to 2.4 percent of a step, measured). A follow that never moves is bit for bit the domain without it, with the seeded turbulence too (commit 8c30823: the noise was keyed by the cell of the window, so a follow at window zero differed from none; it is keyed by the cell of the box the state began in, and a test with turbulence added holds it). A face is asked for room only if the density-weighted air in the smoke nearest it goes toward it (commit 80f70d5), justified by the oracle of smoke at rest (test a_window_does_not_move_against_the_drift_of_its_smoke_to_make_room_behind_it), not by the hero: the hero's window is the same under the first policy (every face asked for room, d87fc65) and this one, -78, -72, -72, -72, -75, -90 over the six times measured with the first and -78, -72, -72, -75, -90 at 1, 1.25, 3, 5 and 5.96 s with this one; a figure of 22 units for the first policy on the hero that an earlier text gave is withdrawn. What a move lets go of is counted in State::lost, never more than the share followLoss asks, and a window never leaves a slab with a cell of an acting source. HERO SCENE (examples/cinematic-impact/hero.scene.xml, follow margin 3, loss 0.001, 1280 x 720, release build, NVIDIA through the GPU queue; the set of frames is Mercurio's, with its MANIFEST): the window moves down 6 units at 1.125 s (the first cell of the grid at y = -78 at 1 s, -72 at 1.25 s and at 3 s, -75 at 5 s, -90 at 5.96 s; sr-eval example pyro_extent, ci build, deterministic). The smoke in the three cells at the top face: 0.2745 at 5.0 s with follow against 0.2954 without; 0.1706 at 5.96 s with follow against 88.54 without (of 2999 and 2996 in all): without follow the plume is cut by the top face, with it it is not. Pixels at 1280 x 720: frame 120 (5.0 s) follow against no follow differ in 355,186 of 921,600 (38.5 percent, largest difference 102, mean 0.832), frame 143 (5.96 s) in 330,453 (35.9 percent, 69, 0.955). THE HASH OF THE t = 3.0 PROBE has three values with three reasons: 24c6ab56... (963b614, the scene without follow), eeb71e14... (d87fc65, follow merged), c8a66483... (from 80f70d5; the same in the release and the ci build, and on 28887eb); the last two differ in 185,284 pixels (20.1 percent, largest 157, mean 0.153), which are attributed to the noise key (8c30823; the hero has turbulence and the window is the same under both policies) unless a measurement says otherwise (a probe at 3.0 s with only 8c30823 would decide and has not been made), and the frames without follow are bit for bit the same before and after them (sha256 a9d92b13... and ea8a614c...). The probe did not return to 24c6ab56..., which a forecast had said it would: the window has moved at 1.125 s, before 3 s, so the frame cannot be the one of the scene without follow.
milestones.limits: A plume has to fit in its window: follow follows the head of the plume only while the stem that joins it to its source, and the smoke that numerical diffusion spreads about it, fit between the faces with the margin; a plume that does not fit is cut as it was, and the remedy is a larger window. A followLoss large enough to let go of the stem loses visible smoke, and a loss of zero never moves a window (the advection leaves a tail that is never exactly zero). The margin (12 cells by default, 3 in the hero) and the loss have no published source; the 12 is the distance from which a plume's top face was measured to have no effect (W02). The hero's frames after the first move of the window are a function of the policy: a change of policy changes them (the hash above is of the scene at a commit, not a fixed reference), and only one probe time (3.0 s) and two frames (120 and 143) were compared. The decision reads every cell once a step on one core.
